newsitem.title: TURKEY: Iran's Rafsanjani visits southeast Turkey.
newsitem.headline: Iran's Rafsanjani visits southeast Turkey.

text.p: Iranian President Akbar Hashemi Rafsanjani visited southeast Turkey on Friday as part of a trip aimed at boosting trade links between the two countries in defiance of U.S. efforts to isolate Tehran.
Rafsanjani said Iran sought to further deepen relations between the two neighbouring Moslem countries, which have warmed since Necmettin Erbakan became Turkey's first Islamist prime minister in June.

"We will bring the relationship between our two countries to a good level that will be an example to the countries of the region," Rafsanjani was quoted as saying by Turkey's state-run Anatolian news agency.
Rafsanjani was speaking as he accompanied Turkish President Suleyman Demirel on a trip to inspect Turkey's Southeast Anatolian Project (GAP), a $32 billion dam and irrigation development.

GAP is at the centre of a dispute between Ankara and its downstream neighbours Syria and Iraq, who say Turkey is hogging the bulk of water from the Tigris and Euphrates rivers that originate on its territory.
The project is key to the future of mainly-Kurdish southeast Turkey, where a 12-year-old armed conflict between security forces and Kurdish rebels has left the economy badly neglected.
"Iranian natural gas will come to this region and play a big role in the development of industry here," said Rafsanjani, who began a four-day visit to Turkey on Thursday.
Turkey signed a $23 billion agreement for the supply of Iranian natural gas over 23 years during a visit by Erbakan to Iran in August on his first major trip abroad as prime minister.
The deal was struck days after U.S. President Bill Clinton signed a law imposing sanctions on any company investing over $40 million a year in the energy industries of Iran or Libya.

On Thursday a senior Turkish official said a preliminary study on construction of a pipeline to carry Iranian oil to Western markets through Turkey's Mediterranean terminal of Ceyhan would be discussed during Rafsanjani's visit.
Erbakan said the two countries hoped to raise trade volume to more than $2 billion in 1997 from $957 million in 1995.

The visit is likely to antagonise the United States, which is a close ally of NATO member Turkey and is trying to isolate Iran, which Washington accuses of sponsoring terrorism. Iran denies the charge.
